text:
maria: Heads-up — I kicked off a gitops apply for the tf-mod that adds cross-region burst_capacity to gpupools and we started seeing node boot failures in eu-west-1.
maria: Error in the node logs: \n```
ERROR: failed to decrypt instance identity: KMS key not found for alias redwood/gpupool/eu-west-1
```

dom: ugh. did the module change the kms alias naming? I remember we added region templating in the last PR.

maria: yeah we switched from `redwood/gpupool/${region}` to `redwood/gpupool/${var.kms_alias_root}/${region}` so the alias in us-west-2 exists, but eu alias wasn't created in the state migration run.

infra-bot: deploy-pipeline: apply started for repo=infra/gpupools branch=feature/cross-region-burst at 2041209800

sre-leah: how many nodes failed? impact on capacity? we have a few workloads pinned to eu-west-1.

maria: ~12 nodes failed to join and ended up in Stopped state; autoscaler then tried to spin new replacements which hit the same KMS error.

tony: rolling apply should've been gated. Did the gitops pipeline run plan-review or straight apply?

dom: pipeline did plan -> auto-apply on merge. The plan had the alias changes but the state migration script that creates missing aliases wasn't run in eu region because of a conditional we forgot.

ops-jen: For now we should: 1) pause auto-apply for gpupools, 2) run a manual plan in eu-west-1 with the migration script to create aliases, 3) retry canary region only. Can someone take step 2?

maria: I'll take it. Quick notes: run from CI runner in eu region, export AWS_REGION=eu-west-1, then `terraform state mv` not required — we just need to create the alias (it’s a separate aws_kms_alias resource). Example snippet: \n```
resource "aws_kms_alias" "gpupool_alias" {
  name          = "alias/redwood/gpupool/${var.kms_alias_root}/${var.region}"
  target_key_id = aws_kms_key.gpupool_key[0].key_id
}
```

dom: also double-check provider aliasing in the module. We had a race where provider.aliases["eu"] didn't get passed to the module in the canary apply, causing the provider lookup to default to us-west creds.

sre-leah: Once aliases are in place, we'll need to drain/recycle the failed nodes. Use `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets` with a 5m timeout for pods with disruption budgets.

tony: Postmortem action items: (a) add a gitops gate for cross-region KMS alias creation, (b) add an automated preflight check that validates kms alias per-region exists before applying gpupool changes, (c) make the module idempotent for alias creation so apply is safe.

ops-jen: +1. Also add a canary flag to the module so the default apply does not flip burst_capacity across all regions in one go. We need a controlled rollout parameter.

maria: manual run started (eu runner) at 2041211200 — creating aliases now. Will update with results.

infra-bot: ci-runner-eu: terraform apply complete for infra/gpupools (eu-west-1) at 2041212800 — 3 resources added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed

maria: aliases created successfully. Follow-up: I triggered a small canary apply to eu-west-1 only and set burst_capacity = 2 (was 8) — nodes came up fine and joined cluster.

sre-leah: great. we'll drain the failed instances and let the canary run for 1h before promoting.

dom: I'll open a PR to revert the provider conditional bug and add provider alias tests to the module's unit tests. Also adding an env-check workflow that runs `aws kms list-aliases --region $REGION | grep redwood/gpupool` as a preflight.

tony: thanks team. putting this on the agenda for the next infra retro. short-term: lock auto-apply on gpupools until we have the preflight in place. :lock:

maria: noted. marking the gitops PR as paused and adding a blocker in the release board.
